Chapter 9: Living with Purpose and Direction.
You know that restless feeling when you’re not sure why you’re here? It’s something so many of us experience—spending years searching for purpose, trying out different roles, and chasing after some deeper meaning.
There’s this fear, isn’t there? The fear of wasting your life. It can be overwhelming, filling you with anxiety and doubt.
Take the story of a man in midlife. On the surface, he had it all—success, achievements, the kind of life most people would envy. But one day, he started questioning everything. Those accomplishments that used to mean so much suddenly felt empty.
One evening, he volunteered at a local shelter. While listening to the stories of people who’d lost almost everything, he was struck by their hope. Despite what they’d been through, they somehow found reasons to believe in tomorrow.
In their resilience, he discovered a new kind of purpose. It wasn’t about ticking off boxes or collecting trophies. It was about serving others, and finding meaning in the simple act of showing up for someone else.
Most of us don’t realize just how often we look for direction in all the wrong places. If you think back to stories from ancient times, you’ll see a pattern—people found their calling not through elaborate plans, but through simple moments of saying yes.
There was a woman, for example, known for her hospitality. She opened her home to strangers, not knowing it would place her right at the heart of a story far bigger than her own.
Or think about a college student, torn about what to study. She felt the weight of her family’s expectations, the pressure to choose something impressive. After months of being stuck, she decided to spend a summer working with kids in her neighborhood.
The joy she found in those little connections opened her eyes. She realized that purpose isn’t about status. It’s about the impact you make, one person at a time.
What really becomes clear is that direction usually comes in small steps. So many people sit around, waiting for a sign, but the real invitation is just to move forward with what you know now. Trust that clarity will come later.
The God who gently whispers your name doesn’t demand perfection. He doesn’t ask for absolute certainty. The real invitation is to live with an open heart—to say yes to opportunities, to serve where there’s a need, and to trust that every step, no matter how small, really does matter.
So, if you’re searching for purpose, here’s what I want you to remember: Start right where you are. You might not see the whole path yet, but every act of love, every moment of kindness, is shaping a story bigger than you can imagine.
In the end, purpose isn’t something you stumble across. It’s something you choose to live, day by day.
